outputs.exact_statement:
There are separable real Banach spaces $X,Y$ and a bijection $\Psi:X\to Y$ such that, for every $s,t\in X$, $$\label{eq:main-bounds}
 \frac4{21}\|s-t\|_X
 \le \|\Psi(s)-\Psi(t)\|_Y
 \le \frac{76}{25}\|s-t\|_X.$$ The space $X$ contains a linearly isometric copy of $c_0(\ell_2)$, while $Y$ contains no closed subspace linearly isomorphic to $c_0(\ell_2)$. In particular, $X$ and $Y$ are not linearly isomorphic.

Let $(M,d,0)$ be a complete pointed metric space, and let $\mu_i\to0$ weakly in $\mathcal F(M)$. For every $\tau>0$, there is a compact $K\subset M$, with $0\in K$, such that $$\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(\mu_i,\mathcal F(K))<\tau\qquad\hbox{for every }i.$$
If $M$ is a superreflexive real Banach space, then $\mathcal F(M)$ is weakly sequentially complete. In particular, this applies to every real Hilbert space $M$.

$Z_Q$ is a Banach space, and it is separable if $A,H$ are separable. The coordinate map $p_i:Z_Q\to A$, $p_i(s)=s_i$, has norm at most $2^i$, and $$J_Q:Z_Q\to c_0(H),\qquad J_Q(s)=(Qs_i)_i,$$ has norm at most one.
If $E$ is a weakly sequentially complete real Banach space, then $\ell_1(E)$ contains no closed subspace linearly isomorphic to ordinary $c_0$.

Let $E,U$ be real Banach spaces, with $E$ weakly sequentially complete, and let $q:E\to U$ be a completely continuous bounded linear operator. Then $Z_q$ contains no closed subspace linearly isomorphic to $c_0(\ell_2)$.

Let $U$ be a separable real Hilbert space, $V=\ell_2$, and $M=U\oplus_2V$, with projections $\pi_U,\pi_V$. Suppose $h:M\to U$ is a bijection with $h(0)=0$ and, for all $x,x'\in M$, $$a\|x-x'\|\le\|h(x)-h(x')\|\le b\|x-x'\|,
 \qquad 0<a\le b<\infty.$$ Let $E=\mathcal F(M)$ and let $q:E\to U$ be the linearization of $D=h-\pi_U$. Suppose $q$ is completely continuous. Give $E\oplus V$ the sum norm, define $$Q_1:E\oplus_1V\to M,\quad Q_1(e,v)=(qe,v),\qquad
 X=Z_{Q_1},\qquad Y=Z_q,$$ and put $L_q=\|q\|$, $K_q=\max\{L_q,1\}$. Then $X,Y$ are separable real Banach spaces and there is a bijection $\Psi:X\to Y$ such that $$\label{eq:criterion-bounds}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Lip}}(\Psi)\le\max\{1+K_q,b\},\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{Lip}}(\Psi^{-1})\le\max\{1+2L_q/a,1/a\}.$$ Moreover, $X$ contains $c_0(V)$ isometrically and $Y$ contains no closed subspace linearly isomorphic to $c_0(V)$.

The identities $qB=hQ_1$ and $Q_1B^{-1}=h^{-1}q$ involve nonlinear maps on both sides. They do not exhibit a map $s:U\to E$ with $qs=\operatorname{id}_U$, Lipschitz or otherwise. In particular, the quotient splitting corollary of Godefroy and Kalton (Godefroy and Kalton 2003, Corollary 3.2) [[GK03](#ref-GK03)] cannot be invoked from these identities.

Let $(M,\rho,0)$ be a complete separable pointed metric space, and let $$U=\left(\bigoplus_{n\ge1}U_n\right)_2$$ be a real Hilbert space with finite-dimensional blocks. Fix an orthonormal basis in every $U_n$, and write $\Pi_{\ge l}$ for projection onto $U_{\ge l}=(\bigoplus_{n\ge l}U_n)_2$. Suppose $D:M\to U$ is Lipschitz with $D(0)=0$, and that for every $m\ge1$ and every distinct $z_1,\ldots,z_m\in M$ there are open neighborhoods $O_j$ of $z_j$, an integer $l\ge1$, and mutually orthogonal coordinate subspaces $H_j\subset U_{\ge l}$ such that $$\label{eq:local-orthogonality}
 \Pi_{\ge l}D(O_j)\subset H_j\qquad(1\le j\le m).$$ A coordinate subspace means the closed span of a subset of the fixed orthonormal basis. Then $$q=\widehat D:\mathcal F(M)\to U$$ is completely continuous.

Let $(M,\rho,0)$ be a pointed metric space, let $z\in M$, and let $\mu_i\to0$ weakly in $\mathcal F(M)$. Suppose $r_i>0$, $r_i\to0$, and $f_i:M\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $$f_i(z)=0,\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{Lip}}(f_i)\le C,\qquad
 f_i(x)=0\quad\hbox{when }\rho(x,z)\ge r_i,$$ where $C$ does not depend on $i$. Then $\langle f_i,\mu_i\rangle\to0$.

There are finite-dimensional Euclidean coordinate spaces $U_n$, $U=(\bigoplus_{n\ge1}U_n)_2$, and a bijection $h:U\oplus_2\ell_2\to U$ fixing zero, such that $$\label{eq:h-bounds}
 \frac{24}{25}\|x-x'\|
 \le\|h(x)-h(x')\|
 \le\frac{26}{25}\|x-x'\|.$$ Moreover, $D=h-\pi_U$ has local orthogonality: for every finite family of distinct points $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ there are neighborhoods $O_j$ of $x_j$, an integer $l$, and mutually orthogonal coordinate subspaces $H_j\subset(\bigoplus_{n\ge l}U_n)_2$ such that $$P_{\ge l}D(O_j)\subset H_j\qquad(1\le j\le m).$$ Here $P_{\ge l}$ is the projection onto blocks with index at least $l$, and a coordinate subspace is the closed span of a subset of the specified orthonormal coordinates.
For every finite family of distinct points of $M$ there are neighborhoods $O_j$ and an integer $l$ such that the coordinate supports of $\{w_n(x):x\in O_j,\ n\ge l\}$ are disjoint for different $j$.
